Which statement about indifference curves is not correct?

options.A: Indifference curves are usually convex to the origin of the diagram.
options.B: Indifference curves can intersect each other.
options.C: The consumer always prefers a higher indifference curve to a lower one.
options.D: The slope of the indifference curve represents the marginal rate of substitution.

questions.questionText: A firm increases its production. When will this result in allocative efficiency?

options.A: when the cost of producing the last extra unit equals the value the consumers place on it
options.B: when the cost of producing the last extra unit is at a minimum
options.C: when the total cost of production equals the value that consumers place on the total product
options.D: when the total revenue reaches a maximum

In a perfectly contestable market, entries and exits are cost-free. In reality, why is this not the case with some firms in contestable markets?

options.A: Firms cannot recover all fixed costs if they cease operations.
options.B: Firms in the industry all operate at the equilibrium level of output.
options.C: Large firms do not have to increase capital to grow.
options.D: Multinational companies always benefit from economies of scale.

questions.questionText: What is an external economy of scale?

options.A: cheaper costs from purchasing large quantities of inputs
options.B: decreased interest rates on borrowed funds
options.D: relevant training facilities at a local college

questions.questionText: A group of producers enter into an agreement to restrict supply or fix the price of a good. What does this describe?

options.A: a cartel
options.D: horizontal integration

questions.questionText: What is meant by a four-firm concentration ratio of 25%?

options.A: The largest four firms’ market share totals 25%.
options.B: The largest four firms have a market share of 25% each.
options.C: There are only four firms in the industry.
options.D: The largest firm has a 25% market share.

options.B: a shift to the right in the demand curve for labour

A government decides to cut the rate of interest in order to stimulate aggregate demand and increase employment. Why might this policy not work in a recession?

options.A: Business confidence is low.
options.C: It leads to an appreciation in the exchange rate.
options.D: It leads to a decrease in the money supply.

questions.questionText: Households in an economy change their consumption behaviour causing the consumption curve to shift from C to C .
How would decreasing interest rates be most likely to reduce unemployment?

options.A: by decreasing the borrowing costs of business
options.B: by decreasing the government’s budget deficit
options.C: by increasing the foreign exchange rate of the currency
options.D: by increasing the opportunity cost of spending

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a curve representing the relationship between a country’s unemployment rate and its inflation rate. inflation rate O unemployment rate Why is it likely that this curve only applies in the short run?

options.A: Any attempt to reduce unemployment will increase inflation.
options.C: Increased inflation leads to expectations of further inflation.
options.D: Increased inflation reduces real wage rates, which increases the demand for labour.

questions.questionText: What is the most likely result of a period of negative actual growth?

options.A: an increase in the surplus of the financial account of the balance of payments
options.B: an increase in the deficit of the current account of the balance of payments
options.C: an increase in the rate of inflation
options.D: an increase in the rate of unemployment

questions.questionText: An economy experiences falling incomes and rising unemployment. The central bank decides to reduce the rate of interest to stimulate economic activity. When would such a policy be most likely to succeed?

options.A: when spending by consumers on goods and services is income elastic
options.B: when spending by firms on capital goods is interest rate elastic
options.C: when the leakage on additional national income is high
options.D: when the overseas demand for exports is price inelastic

questions.questionText: Monetary policy does not usually work immediately. Which time lag is likely to be the least concern to a government whose priority is a rapid domestic impact?

options.A: the time it takes for policymakers to recognise the cause of a problem
options.B: the time it takes for the economy to respond to the introduction of the policy
options.C: the time it takes for the foreign exchange rate to respond to the effect of the policy
options.D: the time it takes to put the chosen policy measure into place

questions.questionText: During a year, a country’s national income in money terms increased by 5%, prices increased by 4% and the total population increased by 2%. What was the approximate change in real income per head?

options.A: a decrease of 1%
options.D: an increase of 2%

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from foreign direct investment in a developing economy?

options.A: an improvement in the developing economy’s trade balance
options.B: an increase in the developing economy’s net investment income
options.C: a reduction in the developing economy’s government tax revenue
options.D: a reduction in wage levels in the developing economy
